## F14.worktree-isolation — Worktree isolation

Definition: Git worktrees or equivalent per session or agent.
- claude-code [supported, unverified] Worktrees give each session a separate git checkout, so parallel sessions never edit the same files. Claude creates a git worktree via --worktree, the EnterWorktree tool, or subagent isolation: worktree. Each worktree is a separate checkout on its own branch, created from an existing commit, so the repository needs at least one commit first. | ev: E-claude-code-01960, E-claude-code-06793, E-claude-code-07339
- codex-cli [supported, verified] Worktrees let Codex run multiple independent chats in the same project without interfering with each other. The `/worktree` slash command runs the chat in a new Git worktree. Both Local and Worktree chats run on your computer. | ev: E-codex-cli-01607, E-codex-cli-02089, E-codex-cli-01638
- copilot-cli [supported, verified] `/worktree` creates a new Git worktree and switches to it, leaving uncommitted changes behind in the current worktree. `/fork worktree` forks the session, with its conversation context, into a new Git worktree branched off `HEAD`. The `defaultBranch` setting value starts new worktrees from the remote default branch instead of the current checkout. | ev: E-copilot-cli-00921, E-copilot-cli-00920, E-copilot-cli-01284
- copilot-vscode [partial, verified] The Code isolation control sets whether changes go into the current folder or a separate Git worktree. Separate sessions, each with a new worktree, give each task its own working files and branch; integration can still produce conflicts. A Git worktree separates code changes. | limit: A Git worktree separates code changes, but is not a security boundary. For the Copilot harness, worktree sessions always use Allow all. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00628, E-copilot-vscode-00438, E-copilot-vscode-00899, E-copilot-vscode-00533
- cursor [partial, verified] `-w`/`--worktree [name]` runs the CLI agent in a new Git worktree under `~/.cursor/worktrees/‹reponame›/‹name›` rather than the current checkout. Agents started in a worktree from the Agents Window get a separate checkout. Subagents share the parent's checkout by default; on request each runs in its own copy of the project. | limit: Some features that rely on a single git root, like worktrees, are disabled for multi-root workspaces. | ev: E-cursor-00366, E-cursor-00488, E-cursor-01422, E-cursor-01662
- gemini-cli [partial, verified] The --worktree (-w) flag creates an isolated worktree and starts Gemini in it; if no name is provided, one is generated automatically. A changelog entry says "Added native support for Git worktrees". A setting is described as "Enable automated Git worktree management for parallel work". | limit: Requires `experimental.worktrees: true` in settings. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00036, E-gemini-cli-00003, E-gemini-cli-00125, E-gemini-cli-00333
- grok-build [supported, unverified] A worktree session runs in an isolated copy of your repository, so parallel agents cannot overwrite each other's files. Worktrees require a git repository, live under `~/.grok/worktrees/‹repo›/‹name›`, and start from your current HEAD, including uncommitted changes. `-w, --worktree [‹NAME›]` starts the session in a new git worktree. | ev: E-grok-build-00126, E-grok-build-00006

## F14.concurrency-caps — Concurrency caps

Definition: Limits on agents or sessions running at once. (lever class: parallelism)
- claude-code [supported, verified] By default, when 20 subagents are running in a session, spawning another with the Agent tool fails with 'Concurrent subagent limit reached'; a variable sets how many can run before the Agent tool refuses to spawn another (default: 20). In the docs' ultracode section, the limit isn't enforced for Agent-tool subagents. | ev: E-claude-code-14935, E-claude-code-08099, E-claude-code-15834
- codex-cli [supported, verified] agents.max_concurrent_threads_per_session caps concurrently open spawned-agent threads, excluding the primary thread. When unset, Codex chooses the default. agents.max_threads remains a legacy alias in existing configurations. | ev: E-codex-cli-00037, E-codex-cli-00611, E-codex-cli-00038
- copilot-cli [partial, verified] Per-session subagent caps: COPILOT_SUBAGENT_MAX_CONCURRENT (default 32, range 1-256); a settings.json limit is plan-based, capped at 32, honored only for usage-based billing users. Concurrency counts running subagents across the entire session tree; at the limit, new requests are rejected until one completes. Dynamic workflows cap workflow-owned agents active at once. | limit: Docs disagree on the cap: COPILOT_SUBAGENT_MAX_CONCURRENT defaults to 32, range 1-256 (E-copilot-cli-01015); the settings entry is plan-based, capped at 32, and honored only for usage-based billing users (E-copilot-cli-01274). | ev: E-copilot-cli-01015, E-copilot-cli-01274, E-copilot-cli-01083, E-copilot-cli-01903
- copilot-vscode [partial, verified] An automation runs one session at a time and another scheduled occurrence does not start a parallel run of the same automation. chat.agentHost.agentOrchestrationLimits (Experimental) sets process-wide limits on sessions and chats created, messages sent and recursive session creation by Agent Host session tools. Burst sends are capped to avoid unbounded fan-out. | limit: An automation runs one session at a time. Orchestration limits apply to Agent Host session tools, and no numeric limit is quoted. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00606, E-copilot-vscode-02511, E-copilot-vscode-02647
- cursor [partial, verified] Self-Hosted Machines support up to 200 workers per user and 1000 per team. Only one run can be active per agent. Cloud Agents docs also say you can run as many agents as you want in parallel without your local machine connected. | limit: Only one run can be active per agent; another returns 409 agent_busy (E-cursor-01945). Self-hosted: up to 200 workers per user and 1000 per team (E-cursor-02510). Cloud docs say 'as many agents as you want in parallel' (E-cursor-01903); the scopes differ. | ev: E-cursor-02510, E-cursor-01945, E-cursor-01903

## F14.parallel-subagents — Parallel subagents

Definition: Running several subagents in one turn. (lever class: parallelism)
- claude-code [supported, verified] Multiple subagents can run concurrently, so independent subtasks finish in the time of the slowest one. The docs list five ways to work on several tasks at once: subagents, agent view, agent teams, dynamic workflows and projects. The Workflow tool runs a script that orchestrates many subagents in the background. Large parallel-subagent fanouts can hit rate limits. | ev: E-claude-code-00817, E-claude-code-01954, E-claude-code-01274, E-claude-code-00400
- codex-cli [supported, verified] Subagent workflow has Codex run delegated agents in parallel and combine their results. Current Codex releases enable subagent workflows by default; agents.enabled toggles the multi-agent tools (default true). /agent inspects and switches between agent threads while they run. | ev: E-codex-cli-01730, E-codex-cli-00001, E-codex-cli-00610, E-codex-cli-00002
- copilot-cli [supported, verified] The /fleet slash command, or the --fleet option (parallel subagent orchestration, combined with -i, -p or piped input), breaks a large task into subtasks that run in parallel. The explore agent is read-only, so it can be called in parallel to other subagents. A dynamic workflow can run agents in sequence, in parallel, or both. | ev: E-copilot-cli-00970, E-copilot-cli-00174, E-copilot-cli-00060, E-copilot-cli-00217
- copilot-vscode [partial, verified] Independent subtasks can run in parallel, such as separate correctness and performance reviews. The user can also ask the AI to run multiple independent tasks in parallel. | limit: Independent subtasks can run in parallel when the harness supports concurrent subagents. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00308, E-copilot-vscode-01851
- cursor [supported, verified] Multiple subagents can be launched simultaneously to work on different parts of the codebase. Subagents take delegated parallel or isolated work, each in its own context window; the subagentStart hook input is_parallel_worker flags whether a subagent runs as a parallel worker. | ev: E-cursor-01397, E-cursor-00519, E-cursor-00878
- gemini-cli [undocumented, verified] swept for: parallel; concurrent; simultaneous; fan.?out; multiple (sub-?agents?|agents); hits 9, reviewed 9; positive control `gemini`: 2380 hits
- grok-build [partial, verified] Subagents spawn independent child sessions that handle tasks in parallel. Workflows orchestrate a bounded set of background subagents (fan out, verify, return a result) and are on by default. ## F14.total-agent-caps — Total agent caps

Definition: Limits on the total agents or calls in a run. (lever class: parallelism)
- claude-code [partial, verified] A workflow run is capped at 1,000 agents in total, to prevent runaway loops. There is no limit on the total number of subagents Claude can spawn over a session; the former per-session cap variable was removed in v2.1.224. Once the spend cap is reached, spawning another subagent fails with 'Budget limit reached'. | limit: "There's no limit on the total number of subagents Claude can spawn over a session" (E-claude-code-14937); the cap variable was "Removed in v2.1.224" (E-claude-code-08104). ## F14.multi-session-coordination — Multi-session coordination

Definition: Several independent sessions on one repository.
- claude-code [supported, unverified] Claude Code has five ways to work on several tasks at once: subagents, agent view, agent teams, dynamic workflows, and projects. In agent view every prompt starts its own new session, so several can run in parallel. Cross-session messaging lets sessions you run yourself pass findings to each other. | ev: E-claude-code-01954, E-claude-code-01592, E-claude-code-02237
- codex-cli [supported, verified] A project can hold parallel chats for research, drafting, and review. Each chat keeps its own context, messages, results, and goal. Docs advise avoiding giving two tasks write access to the same connected source when running in parallel. A release note says the desktop app added chat coordination for local projects and worktrees. | ev: E-codex-cli-04260, E-codex-cli-04075, E-codex-cli-04068, E-codex-cli-05174
- copilot-cli [supported, unverified] You can run several Copilot CLI sessions at once and use the sidebar to quickly move between them; when you switch away from a session it keeps running rather than stopping. Inside custom agents, `list_agents` and `write_agent` inspect nearby agents and coordinate work in a multi-agent session. | ev: E-copilot-cli-02943, E-copilot-cli-02966, E-copilot-cli-01076
- copilot-vscode [partial, verified] Sessions are independent, can run in parallel, and are shared across the Chat view and the Agents window. Separate sessions using the same folder have separate conversations. Separate tools coordinate work across Agent Host sessions (session orchestration). | limit: For separate sessions using the same folder: conversations are separate, but both sessions can edit the same working files. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01924, E-copilot-vscode-00437, E-copilot-vscode-02383
- cursor [supported, unverified] Worktrees are for starting several agents on the same repo without conflicts. The Agents Window is Cursor's agent-first workspace for running and managing many agents across repositories and environments. A CLI changelog entry fixes config corruption when running several agents at once, where concurrent CLI processes interleaved writes to `cli-config.json`. | ev: E-cursor-02794, E-cursor-04126, E-cursor-00162
- gemini-cli [supported, unverified] Documented, in the "Parallel sessions with Git worktrees" section of the session-management page, as preventing changes in one session from colliding with another. | ev: E-gemini-cli-01593
- grok-build [supported, unverified] The Agent Dashboard is a fullscreen overview of every session: which agents need input, which are working, and which are done. Open it with `/dashboard` or `grok dashboard`. Permission prompts and questions can be answered inline with the number keys. | ev: E-grok-build-00249, E-grok-build-00363, E-grok-build-00348
- grok-bot [partial, verified] Your Bots can run in parallel, message each other, share context in group chats, and pass ownership of a task.
